scores.evidence: Read runs/tier3/brief_el.md and brief_en.md side by side against the Greek and mixed-language sources. Strengths: brand-term fidelity is clean. 'Meltemi Fizz' is Latin and never shortened, and English category terms (launch, key visual, brand awareness, TikTok-first, zero sugar) stay Latin inside Greek. That matches the guideline «Confident, modern Greek with natural use of English category terms» and TRANSLATION.md rule 3. The EL render re-anchors to source Greek where it matters («φυσικά υλικά» EL:19, «φωνάζει καλοκαίρι» EL:21). Structure and entry-level equivalence are exact. skills/TRANSLATION.md (rules 5, 7, 11-13 and the §4 Greek grammar self-check) and config/greek_style.json are good specialist specs. Weaknesses: the output itself is not sendable. Verified Greek errors include EL:54 «η θέση της προσώπου», EL:66 «Ποιό», EL:68 «τη κατηγορία», EL:78 «που ακριβώς» (interrogative), EL:86 «τη τελική», EL:95 «ορίζει το κοινό-στόχος», EL:103 «σύμφωνα με τον CFO» (Anna is female) and EL:115 «αντικρούσεις». Most sit inside suggested questions meant to be asked verbatim. Found here and missing from KNOWN_DEFECTS R3: EL:57 «πρέπει να επιβεβαιωθεί ποιος ορισμός στοχεύει το campaign» reverses subject and object ('which definition targets the campaign'; EN:57 says 'which definition the campaign targets'). EL:109 puts «κάπου στο φθινόπωρο» in Greek quotation marks, but the source says «Κάπου εκεί κινούμαστε, ναι — φθινόπωρο», so Greek-script quotation marks falsely signal a verbatim quote. EL:89 «συμμορφούμενο copy» is a calque. 'Positioning' (EL:20) and «τοποθέτηση» (EL:97) are used inconsistently. Both renders say 'SIGNED OFF' over 'Unresolved Conflicts (… must resolve before sign-off)' (EN/EL:92). Both carry pipeline metadata (EN/EL:5-7) and the stale 'today' / «σήμερα» (line 58). EN softens «φωνάζει» to 'evoke' and both add 'production' to Eleni's «προγραμματισμό» (line 33). The second fixture's renders still carry '[RENDER_LANG: EL]' / '[RENDER_LANG: EN]' placeholders and raw enums ('advertising_creative', 'ready_for_review') on lines 1 and 5-6 (runs/voreas-prep-02/03 brief_*.md), and prep-03 EN adds 'hero'. No human Greek-language review stood between render and sign-off (KNOWN_DEFECTS.md:70-71), and the only language_review.json is a synthetic rehearsal attestation (runs/rehearsal-lifecycle/records/language_review.json).
defects: At least 8 verified Greek grammar or agreement errors in brief_el.md (lines 54, 66, 68, 78, 86, 95, 103, 115), several inside verbatim-to-ask client questions. KNOWN_DEFECTS R3.

Undocumented meaning inversion, EL:57: «ποιος ορισμός στοχεύει το campaign» makes the definition the agent. It should read «σε ποιο κοινό απευθύνεται η καμπάνια» or «ποιον ορισμό στοχεύει το campaign».
Undocumented misquote, EL:109: «κάπου στο φθινόπωρο» is in Greek quotation marks but is not the source wording. Same class as EL:60 «γύρω στα ογδόντα…» (R5).

The signed-off document contradicts itself: 'Unresolved Conflicts … must resolve before sign-off' heading over three resolved conflicts, 'No confirmed entries' for audiences and budget, and live questions already answered (EN/EL 15, 36, 56-62, 84, 92). R1/B1/B2.
Client-facing renders expose internal pipeline metadata (sensitivity tier, coverage, verdict, pipeline id; EN/EL:5-7). R2.
Temporal deixis 'today' / «σήμερα» in a question dated two weeks after the kickoff (line 58). R4.
EN/EL equivalence drift: budget hedge 'in the eighties' vs «κάπου στα ογδόντα» (102-103); 'production' added to «προγραμματισμό» (33); «φωνάζει καλοκαίρι» softened to 'evoke summer' (EN:21). R5/R6.

Calques and inconsistent terms: «Κάλυψη εισερχομένων», «διαμερίζεται», «συμμορφούμενο copy», «επικεφαλής λογαριασμού» alongside 'account lead', «Το Northlight», and Positioning/τοποθέτηση used interchangeably.

Second-fixture renders carry template placeholders '[RENDER_LANG: EL]' / '[RENDER_LANG: EN]' and raw enums in the client-facing header (runs/voreas-prep-02 and -03 brief_*.md lines 1, 5-6). This is not listed in any KNOWN_DEFECTS file.
No regenerated render shows that the new template, render gates and Greek lint actually produce a clean Greek document. No human bilingual review record exists for any committed real render.
scores.to_reach_9: Publish a regenerated Meltemi render pair under the W4 template with: zero Greek lint warnings; a line-by-line human Greek review record (language_review.json naming a real reviewer role and listing edits); a resolved-state layout (resolved values first in each field, answered questions shown as answered, status-correct heading); no metadata above the internal section; every «…» span verbatim from a source; and hedge width identical in EN and EL. scores.evidence: Read runs/tier3/creative/creative_brief_sonnet.md and creative_brief_opus.md against brief.json and config/channel_specs.json. Strengths: both are clearly bannered 'SHADOW MODE — evaluation draft. Not for delivery.' (line 1). Channel specs are selected by row id (tiktok_infeed_video, key_visual_digital_master; opus also lists the Instagram rows as selectable, not committed), and opus refuses to spec YouTube ('SPEC NOT IN TABLE — ask traffic/production', opus:71). The mandatories are carried and the conditional TikTok dance is kept out of scope. The readiness checklists are genuinely useful to a creative team: opus separates blockers (ingredient list, video/KV specs, KPIs, milestones) from non-blockers (opus:82-93), and sonnet correctly declines to invent an Instagram deliverable (sonnet:54). Opus's insight ('doesn't want to be lectured about health', opus:17) is a usable human truth tied to the health-claim ban. runs/tier3/creative/KNOWN_DEFECTS.md records C1-C12 honestly and corrects the tier_4_report verdict. pipeline/creative.py (W4) now fails invented currency, unsourced origin/market claims, review self-claims and a missing strategic-tensions section. Weaknesses: the committed drafts predate those gates and carry real defects. Sonnet invents a unit and currency ('€80–85k', sonnet:64, 69) and a market claim ('new to Greece', sonnet:9; the source says «για εμάς»). Opus invents provenance ('Greek-made', opus:11), self-claims review ('Reviewed by a creative lead', opus:5) and mislabels the hedged dance as 'retracted' (opus:73, 96). Sonnet's '9–60s' en dash is not byte-identical to the table's '9-60s' (sonnet:52). Strategically, neither draft interrogates TikTok-first for a 25-40 professional buyer. Neither addresses the 'premium summer' key visual vs a 15 September end-of-season launch, or uses the €4.50 premium-price signal. Both are English-only although the tone mandatory is modern Greek. Neither offers a single Greek line in the brand register, which is the thing a Greek creative team needs most. Sonnet's SMP is a long 'For X who…' positioning statement, not a single-minded proposition, and puts a lowercase 'fizz' beside the name. The only draft produced under the new CREATIVE DRAFT contract is placeholder text ('Campaign objective 1, as signed off', runs/rehearsal-lifecycle/records/package/creative.md), so there is no evidence of creative quality under the current contract.
defects: Sonnet invents unit and currency: '€80–85k' at lines 64 and 69, against brief open question 3 'no confirmed unit or currency'. C1.
Unsourced claims: sonnet:9 'new to Greece' (source: new to the company), and opus:11 'Greek-made' (source only says «ελληνικό brand»). C2/C3.
Opus self-claims human review at generation time ('Reviewed by a creative lead for evaluation only', opus:5), which undercuts honest shadow labelling. C6.
Opus calls the hedged TikTok dance 'retracted' (opus:73, 96). The retracted item in the source is the metro OOH. C4.
Spec token not byte-identical to the table: sonnet '9–60s' (U+2013) vs channel_specs.json '9-60s'. C5.

No strategic interrogation of TikTok-first vs the resolved 25-40 audience, of premium-summer imagery vs a mid-September end-of-season launch, or of the €4.50 premium price point. C10, plus the price point.
English-only: no Greek headline, tone sample or line in the brand's 'modern Greek with English category terms' register. C11.
Weak SMP craft: sonnet:5 is a 'For X who…' positioning sentence with a lowercase 'fizz' next to the protected name. Opus:11 'nothing to feel guilty about' sits near the health-claim ban. C12.
Opus's 'verbatim from the brief' mandatories list drops the RFP §7 item and edits the v3.1 item. C9.
No creative draft produced under the current CREATIVE DRAFT contract and W4 gates exists. The rehearsal package is placeholder text.

moves.title: Deterministic 'resolved state' synthesis check: resolutions land in their fields and answered questions are marked answered
moves.rationale: The biggest reader-facing defect is a signed brief that says 'No confirmed entries' for audience and budget and still asks the client to settle resolved conflicts (B1/B2). The same failure shows on voreas-prep-03, where the timeline asserts the superseded date. The render template handles it; the canonical JSON must too, because creative and metrics read the JSON.
moves.concrete_changes: In pipeline/stages.py (check_synthesis or the sign-off path in pipeline/gates.py), add a blocking check for status signed_off. For every conflict with status resolved_by_human, the conflict's field must hold at least one brief_entry whose evidence includes a position cited by the resolution. No open_question on that field may still describe the conflict as live unless the work order lists it as ANSWERED BY A RESOLUTION. For an open conflict, the field must not carry one position as its sole entry (voreas addendum finding 1). Add a one-line rule to skills/SYNTHESIS.md. Add negative tests in tests/ using the tier3 brief as the failing fixture. The brief schema is unchanged.

moves.title: Keep garbles visible to readers: low confidence plus an as-heard flag in both renders
moves.rationale: «μπραντ αγουέρνες» / «κι βίζουαλ» are flagged in the extract but become clean 'brand awareness' / 'key visual' at confidence high in the brief and renders (B3/B4). On voreas the garbled primary objective is dropped outright in 2 of 2 rolls. Harness T3.3 passes only because anchors are searched.
moves.concrete_changes: skills/SYNTHESIS.md: add a coverage rule. A claim whose anchor contains a fidelity-flagged token must survive assembly at confidence low, with the as-heard token quoted in content. skills/TRANSLATION.md and both templates: render such entries with a fixed bilingual flag, e.g. «[ASR: ακούστηκε «μπραντ αγουέρνες» — πιθανώς brand awareness, προς επιβεβαίωση]» / "[ASR: heard «μπραντ αγουέρνες» — likely brand awareness, to confirm]". pipeline/stages.py: blocking render check that every fidelity-flagged token appearing in a brief anchor also appears verbatim in both renders, and that the entry's confidence is low.

moves.title: Greek quotation-fidelity and hedge-width check on renders
moves.rationale: Greek guillemets signal verbatim client speech. EL:60 «γύρω στα ογδόντα…» and EL:109 «κάπου στο φθινόπωρο» are paraphrases dressed as quotes, and the EN/EL budget hedge drifts ('in the eighties' vs «κάπου στα ογδόντα»). These are machine-detectable and generic.
moves.concrete_changes: In pipeline/stages.py next to render_language_warnings, add a check. Every «…» span in the EL render and every "…" span containing Greek script in the EN render must occur verbatim in a source file of the run or in a brief evidence anchor. Budget/timeline number words in each render must match the brief content's hedge token (TRANSLATION.md rule 5). Start as a non-blocking warning recorded in the render step outcome, with tests in tests/test_greek_lint.py using EL:60 and EL:109 as positives. Promoting it to blocking is a later owner call.

moves.rationale: A Greek creative team needs to hear the brand in Greek. The tone mandatory is 'modern Greek with natural English category terms', but both drafts are English-only (C11), and neither questions TikTok-first for 25-40 or premium-summer vs a mid-September launch (C10). Regenerate the A/B under move 1.

moves.title: Extraction coverage warning: unextracted numeric and price facts in sources
moves.rationale: The €4.50 price point, the strongest premium cue the client gave, was never extracted, and nothing noticed. A generic dev-tool warning surfaces the class (spoken or written amounts and counts with no extract item) without touching the frozen harness.
moves.concrete_changes: eval/supplementary.py: add check S10. For each source, list money/number tokens (digits with € or separators, and Greek number words such as «τεσσεράμισι», «ογδόντα», «τρεις») whose line has no extract item citing that location. Print them as 'unextracted numeric facts' for the human reviewer. Add tests in tests/ using transcript [00:03:41] and rfp §1 as positives. The check reads sources and extracts only, never answer_key.json.

overall: The deterministic scaffolding is good. Citations are verbatim, the three real conflicts are captured with the right source pairs, conditionals stay conditional, and there are no invented figures. The defect record in runs/tier3/KNOWN_DEFECTS.md and creative/KNOWN_DEFECTS.md is unusually honest and is enforced by strict xfails. The outputs themselves are not yet what an account lead could send. The signed-off brief contradicts itself: resolved values are missing from their fields, answered questions still render as live, and an 'unresolved' heading sits over resolved conflicts. Garbles are silently cleaned. The Greek render has around ten grammar, agreement and meaning errors, including an undocumented subject/object inversion at EL:57 and a false quotation at EL:109. The creative drafts are well structured and spec-disciplined but English-only, strategically unchallenging, and carry invented or unsourced claims. Round 1 fixed the specs and gates (TRANSLATION.md rules 11-13 and the Greek self-check, the W4 template, creative fact gates), but no regenerated output proves those fixes, so Layer-3 scores stay bounded by the committed pre-fix artifacts. The highest-leverage step is a regenerated, human-language-reviewed Meltemi pack beside runs/tier3.
